The Terraform key_name variable refers to an AWS key pair name, not a private key file or secret material. No certificate or key contents are exposed.
launch_specification.key is a Terraform loop key used to choose a subnet. It is not a certificate, private key, or credential.

The VPC ID is read from AWS describe_vpcs for a network cost optimization workflow. This inventory access is expected for implementing VPC endpoints and is not hidden or malicious.
The SQL join combines cost records with resource tags for cost allocation reporting. It does not perform system reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Optimize Cloud Costs Across AWS, Azure, and GCP
content.value_statement: Cloud teams often overspend because waste, rightsizing gaps, and weak tagging are hard to track. This skill guides cost analysis, savings plans, budgets, alerts, and safer optimization workflows.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes cloud costs by service, resource, trend, and waste category.
Recommends rightsizing for compute, databases, containers, serverless functions, and storage.
Plans savings with reservations, Savings Plans, spot instances, storage tiers, and network changes.
Designs budget alerts, tagging policies, allocation reports, and executive cost dashboards.
Includes rollback-focused guidance for resizing, deletion, and production cost controls.
limitations: Requires accurate billing, utilization, tagging, and resource inventory data.
Requires provider permissions and human approval before infrastructure changes.
Sample code must be adapted, tested, and reviewed before production use.
Does not replace formal FinOps governance, security review, or vendor pricing review.

use_cases.title: Reduce Monthly Cloud Spend
use_cases.description: Find waste, idle resources, and quick savings across recent billing data.

use_cases.title: Plan Safer Rightsizing
use_cases.description: Create resize recommendations with risk levels, backup checks, and rollback steps.

use_cases.title: Improve Cost Governance
use_cases.description: Define tagging, budgets, alerts, dashboards, and review cadences for accountable spending.

prompt_templates.title: Find Quick Savings
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cost review with billing exports or console summaries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these cloud cost details for the last 30 days. Identify quick wins, estimate savings, and list risks for each change.

prompt_templates.title: Create Rightsizing Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review using utilization metrics and resource inventory.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these compute, database, storage, and utilization metrics. Recommend rightsizing actions with priority, expected savings, validation steps, and rollback plans.

prompt_templates.title: Build Cost Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced governance setup for budget owners and platform teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cost control plan for this cloud account. Include budgets, alerts, tagging rules, ownership reports, and escalation thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Multi-Cloud Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture review across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-cloud architecture and spending profile. Propose savings across commitments, spot usage, storage tiers, network traffic, and database scaling.

output_examples.input: A team shares monthly AWS costs, EC2 utilization, RDS metrics, and storage volumes.
output_examples.output: A prioritized savings report with idle resources, rightsizing actions, monthly savings estimates, risk notes, and rollback requirements.

output_examples.input: A platform team asks for stronger cost governance across production and staging accounts.
output_examples.output: A governance plan covering tags, budgets, alerts, owner reporting, approval rules, and a monthly optimization cadence.

output_examples.input: An engineering manager needs an executive view of cloud spend trends.
output_examples.output: A dashboard outline with service totals, trend changes, anomaly notes, savings backlog, and accountable cost centers.

best_practices: Validate cost recommendations against production risk, service owners, and rollback requirements.
Use recent billing data with utilization metrics before resizing or deleting resources.
Track savings with tags, owners, budgets, and recurring review meetings.
anti_patterns: Deleting or resizing production resources without backups, monitoring, and rollback plans.
Optimizing only list prices while ignoring performance, reliability, and operational effort.
Using untagged cost data to assign ownership or enforce budget accountability.

faq.question: What cloud providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, and GCP cost optimization patterns, with many examples focused on AWS services.

faq.question: Can it make infrastructure changes automatically?
faq.answer: It provides implementation guidance and sample workflows. Production changes still require permissions, testing, and approval.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide billing exports, resource inventory, utilization metrics, tags, account context, and business constraints.

faq.question: Does it support database cost optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide database rightsizing, storage review, scaling options, and reservation planning.

faq.question: How does it balance cost and reliability?
faq.answer: It asks for risk assessment, staging validation, backup checks, and rollback plans before changes.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for FinOps review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare analysis and recommendations, but teams should review business impact and governance decisions.
